pages.text: "No green! Take out the seaweed!" Dari pushed seaweed to the edge of his soup bowl and ate only white fish and broth. Beside him, baby sibling Kongal happily ate green seaweed porridge.
"It's too slippery!" Only white food remained in Dari's bowl. Mom looked a little worried. Kongal ate another spoonful of green porridge.
Next morning, Dari had no energy. His tail felt heavy when he tried to hop onto the shore rocks. "Where did my strength go?"
Mom carried Kongal and took Dari to the rocks' edge. Below, a green seaweed forest swayed underwater. "Wow..." Dari lowered his nose over the sea.
Mom whispered, "Green hides strength. Fish that eat seaweed swim so fast!" A school darted among the fronds. Really? Dari swallowed eagerly.
At dinner, Mom set down soup full of green seaweed and sang, "Green is yummy, too!" Kongal ate green porridge and bounced. Dari gazed into his bowl.
Bravely, Dari slurped seaweed. "Oh! Soft!" He chewed fish and shellfish, too. Better than expected! "Green is yummy, too!"
How strange! His heavy tail felt light, and he lifted his front end high. Dari slapped his tail flippers. His strength was back!
Next dinner, Dari called first. "Green soup today, Mom! One, a green bite! Two, a white bite! Three, a bite of everything!" Mom smiled.
Mom kissed his cheek. "Eating green helped you grow strong!" Green is yummy, too! Dari hopped happily on the shore rocks again.
